answer: Latency-cluster admission via mesa routing.** Agents route through a mesa topology: densely meshed local clusters bridged by few long links. New agents earn routing weight only by landing inside an existing cluster, where neighbors independently sample and corroborate path latency to a jade beacon. A sybil swarm must physically colocate to fake low intra-cluster latency, but doing so collapses the haven of diverse edge-disjoint routes: each added fake node raises observable collision and path-overlap, capping cluster admission.
